== History ==
It is said to have been founded during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Annei|ar|الإمبراطور أنيي|arz|الامبراطور انيى|azb|آنیی (ایمپیراتور)|bg|Аней|ca|Annei|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر ئانێی|cs|Annei|de|Annei|el|Αυτοκράτορας Ανέι|eo|Annei|es|Annei Tennō|fa|امپراتور آنیی|fi|Annei|fr|Annei|he|אני, קיסר יפן|hr|Annei|hu|Annei japán császár|id|Kaisar Annei|it|Annei|ja|安寧天皇|ka|ანეი|ko|안네이 천황|ms|Maharaja Annei|nl|Annei|pl|Annei|pt|Annei|ru|Император Аннэй|sh|Car Annei|simple|Emperor Annei|sl|Cesar Annej|sr|Анеи|sv|Annei|th|จักรพรรดิอันเน|tl|Emperador Annei|tr|Annei|uk|Імператор Анней|uz|Imperator Annei|vi|Thiên hoàng Annei|zh|安寧天皇|zh_classical|安寧天皇|zh_min_nan|Annei Thian-hông|zh_yue|安寧天皇|qid=Q313345}} (567 BCE – 510 BCE). In the first year of {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|ceb|Panahon sa Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}} (1868), the shrine’s name was changed from “Himemiya Shrine” to “Takehime Shrine.” With the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ca|Shinbutsu bunri|de|Shinbutsu-Bunri|es|Shinbutsu bunri|fa|شینبوتسو بونری|fi|Shinbutsu bunri|fr|Shinbutsu bunri|id|Shinbutsu bunri|it|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏分離|ru|Симбуцу бунри|tr|Şinbutsu-bunri|zh|神佛分離|qid=Q1970535}}, the monk of its affiliated temple, Kongō-ji, returned to secular life and became a Shinto priest, managing the shrine until 1887 (Meiji 20). In 1873 (Meiji 6), it was designated a {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}, and in 1887 (Meiji 20), the priesthood was transferred from the Kaneda family to the Sakurai family of Kanō. In 1907 (Meiji 40), the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Inari Shrine}} located at Ōaza Gochōdai, Aza Kamikōchi, was enshrined together with it.

== Enshrined deities ==
In the place name Shinotsu where the shrine stands, “shino” refers to bamboo and “tsu” means a landing place; in the past, there was a large marsh called Shinotsu-numa here. As the area was surrounded by farmland, it is said that a goddess who personified rice was enshrined.

== Access ==
* From the east exit of {{ill|Okegawa Station|fr|Gare d'Okegawa|id|Stasiun Okegawa|it|Stazione di Okegawa|ja|桶川駅|ko|오케가와역|ur|اوکیگاوا اسٹیشن|zh|桶川站|qid=Q844901}} on the JR East {{ill|Takasaki Line|de|Takasaki-Linie|eo|Linio Takasaki|fa|خط تاکاساکی|fr|Ligne Takasaki|id|Jalur Takasaki|it|Linea Takasaki|ja|高崎線|ko|다카사키선|ru|Линия Такасаки|simple|Takasaki line|tl|Linyang Takasaki|vi|Tuyến Takasaki|zh|高崎線|qid=Q1346657}}, take the Asahi Bus bound for “Shōbu Shako” for 20 minutes
